---
title: "A default value is computed when it is first used, not when the function is called"
ref: FUN-14
categories: [Functions]
impact: silencieux
extrait: '(function(x, n = length(x)) { x <- x[-1]; n })(1:3)'
reponse: '2'
attendu: "`\"2 values kept out of 3 received\"`"
versions: "All"
source: "General R knowledge"
---

::: {.piege}
```{r}
describe <- function(x, n_received = length(x)) {
  x <- x[!is.na(x)]
  sprintf("%d values kept out of %d received", length(x), n_received)
}
describe(c(4, NA, 8))

n <- 10
first_n <- function(x, n = n) {
  head(x, n = n)
}
first_n(letters)
```
:::

## Why

R evaluates arguments lazily. A default value is an expression, evaluated inside the function the first time the argument is used. Here, `n_received` is only used on the last line, after `x` has lost its `NA`: `length(x)` then gives 2.

The same rule explains the error of `first_n()`. The default `n = n` is looked up inside the function, where `n` is the argument being computed, and not the `n` of the workspace. R reports a "recursive default argument reference".

## The remedy

Do not overwrite an argument that another default depends on, or evaluate the default at the start of the function with `force()`.

::: {.piege}
```{r}
describe <- function(x, n_received = length(x)) {
  force(n_received)
  kept <- x[!is.na(x)]
  sprintf("%d values kept out of %d received", length(kept), n_received)
}
describe(c(4, NA, 8))
```
:::
